A model rocket’s height is recorded during a launch. The height after $x$ seconds, in meters, is given by the function $H(x).$ The graph of $H(x)$ is shown above.  

Approximate the rate of change when $x=16$ using a backward difference approximation with step size $h=12.$ Do not round the answer.

*Hint: Assume that the graph passes through the points with integer $y$-coordinates when $x=4$ and $x=16.$*

The estimated rate of change when $x=16$ is

![](/home/jake/Developer/Course_Academy/reference/mathacademy/question-capture/14058551/assets/1fcdf0d68d78cba445d1e3ecfeec237ee4e33d7c74cb3b292593fe8b717fe6b8.png)

Peter notices that the total number of eggs produced on his farm $t$ weeks after the beginning of his observations is given by the function $N(t).$ The graph of $N(t)$ is shown above.

Approximate the rate at which the number of produced eggs increases when $t=5$ using a backward difference approximation with step size $h=1.$
feedback.worked_solution:
We use the backward difference approximation formula

$$
{N}^{′}(t)≈\frac{N(t)-N(t-h)}{h},
$$

 
at the point $t=5.$ Applying the above formula with $t=5$ and $h=1$ gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{N}^{′}(5) & ≈\frac{N(5)-N(5-1)}{1} \\  & =\frac{N(5)-N(4)}{1} \\  & =\frac{800-600}{1} \\  & =200.\end{aligned}
$$

So, the rate of increase is $200\,\text{eggs}/\text{week}.$
